newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DE KLERK SETS TEAM FOR S.AFRICA OPPOSITION DRIVE.
newsitem.headline: DE KLERK SETS TEAM FOR S.AFRICA OPPOSITION DRIVE.

text.p: South African National Party leader F.W. de Klerk on Wednesday named Roelf Meyer to lead an initiative to form a broad grouping of moderates to fight the African National Congress in elections in 1999.
De Klerk told a news conference Meyer would quit the post of party secretary-general to head a team of two blacks, a Coloured and two other whites from the party dedicated to the initiative.

"The process must lead to a realignment of politics in South Africa, a process aimed at bringing together a majority of moderate South Africans in a political movement which can challenge the ANC at the polls," de Klerk said.
He said the National Party, while leading the realignment initiative, would at least for the time being continue to exist and would seek to improve its effectiveness.
At some stage in the future the party might cease to exist as a separate entity, subsuming itself in the broader opposition movement, de Klerk said.

"We will unbundle our structures, we will regear our system so that without too much red tape we will establish a capacity... to actively pursue this important goal (of forming a broad political movement)," he said.
"By the end of 1997, hopefully the country could see the birth of a new political movement."
De Klerk said the current dominance of the ANC -- which won 62 percent of the vote in the last election in April 1994 -- was a threat to multi-party democracy.
